title: Teeth and the tongue start mechanical digestion, and saliva starts chemical digestion
summary: OpenStax says teeth and the tongue begin mechanical digestion in the mouth, and saliva begins chemical digestion.
body: OpenStax says that in the mouth, the tongue and the teeth begin mechanical digestion, and saliva begins chemical digestion. The chapter lists teeth as accessory structures, not as part of the food tube itself. Chewing breaks pieces smaller. Saliva starts the chemical work. This card is that mouth job. It does not say when the first tooth arrives.

sources.title: 23.1 and 23.3, chapter review
sources.author: OpenStax
sources.note: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology, first edition, web view, CC BY 4.0. Paraphrase: teeth and tongue begin mechanical digestion; saliva begins chemical digestion; teeth are accessory structures.
